To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the K7 residues of the CTD of human RNAPIIA are modified by mono-, di- and tri-methy- lation and acetylation, and these modifications occur in the context of phosphorylation of the CTD.
the K7 residues in the CTD of RNAPII are subject to acetylation, and mono-, di-, tri-methylation, which are differentially associated with the phosphorylation status of the CTD.
K7me1, 2, and 3 are associated with phosphorylated and acetylated CTD, respectively, and that K7me2 is associated with transcription initiation sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of new posttranslational modifications in the CTD of human RNAPIII and the elucidation of their biological function.
understanding the mechanisms by which the CTD code regulates transcription and how it is altered in disease.
the dynamic modification of heptads with the consensus sequence of RNA polymerase C-terminal domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
K7me1 is associated with phosphorylated and K7me2 with non-phosphorylate CTD, and K7ac is associated only with phosphorylated CDT.
the K7me marks are associated with RNAPII0 and are not present in RNAPIIa, but the exact mechanism of this regulation is not yet known.
the K7me2/3 modifications are present in the phosphorylated form of the CTD, whereas the K7me and K7ac are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the K7me marks of RNAPII CTD have been discovered and that they are present at the transcriptional initiation sites of active genes.
we identified novel lysine modifications of the C-terminal domain of human RNA polymerase II that are dynamically regulated in vivo.
the CTD of RNA polymerase (pol) II undergoes dynamic modifications by acetylation and methylation at the heptapeptide consensus repeat YSPTSPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the K7me2 mark is associated with RNAPII engaged in transcription.
we have discovered a new modification in the CTD that is associated with phosphorylated RNAPII and is enriched at the transcription start site of genes.
the heptad repeat consensus of the CTD is not the exclusive site of modification, and that the K7 residue in particular can be modified by mono-, di-, or tri-methylation and acetylated.
